About me

Hey, I’m Freddie.

I am a UX/UI designer who believes that strategic thinking, creativity and problem solving are all key elements that create enjoyable and delightful user centred experiences.

With my background in music and streaming I developed vital skills in live mediation, mentoring and motivational speaking. In addition to this, for the last 8 years I’ve been beekeeping, where patience and attention to detail have helped me build my own apiary.

The scenic route to design.

Music & streaming

I learned to read a room. Live mediation, mentoring and public speaking taught me how people think, listen and react.

Beekeeping

Eight years of keeping bees taught me patience, observation and attention to detail, and I built my own apiary along the way.

UX/UI design

Now I bring all of it to design: listening first, then shaping simple, human experiences.

Design with people at the centre.

Understand

I start by talking to people and digging into the problem, so I know what really needs solving before I design anything.

Design

I turn what I learn into wireframes and prototypes that are simple to use and easy to follow.

Refine

I test with real users, fix what is confusing, and keep improving until it is clear, simple and accessible.

/teaching-experience:
T e a c h i n g U X D e s i g n

Teaching and mentoring aspiring UX designers through online courses, hands-on workshops and real-world projects.

Where I’ve taught

A global tech school that has helped over two million people learn in-demand skills and launch tech careers. I taught live online UX design courses there, guiding small cohorts through hands-on, project-based learning.

A Stockholm school of communication, design and technology, with bachelor’s, portfolio and online programmes. I shared my UX design experience with its students.

Delivering practical UX skills

I taught UX design courses online, guiding students through the full design process from research and ideation to prototyping, testing and presenting. Alongside the core curriculum, I created my own Figma workshops, ran interactive exercises, provided feedback and supported students on their projects.

Custom workshops and group activities

Alongside the core curriculum, I created and delivered my own Figma workshops and collaborative group activities to help students put theory into practice. These sessions encouraged students to explore ideas, share perspectives and learn from one another.

Providing support for students

I provided ongoing support through 1:1 mentoring sessions, personalised feedback and practical guidance throughout students’ projects, building their confidence and encouraging them to think critically about their design decisions.

What I learned

Kind, specific feedback builds confidence

Students grew fastest when feedback was personal, patient and practical. It built their confidence as much as their skills.

Doing beats explaining

Hands-on Figma workshops and group activities helped students put theory into practice far better than talking through it.

Teaching sharpens my own design

Explaining the design process step by step made me clearer about my own decisions and how I communicate them.

/alta-flora:
Client project · Healthtech · 3 week sprint

Alta Flora

A three week design sprint for Alta Flora’s medical tracking app EVA. In this project I worked in a team of four UX Designers, myself, Scarlet Eadie, Jamie Curtis and Helena Saez.

The client

Who are Alta Flora?

Alta Flora built an app (EVA) for patients consuming legal prescription medical cannabis in the UK in 2019 and released it into the app store in Nov 2020. Now they have expanded to all types of medication, not just cannabis based. EVA is a free app, helping you track your medication and symptoms in order to aid communication with your doctor and improve quality of life.

The brief

Brief

We were approached by Alta flora who wanted their users to find a way to effectively and intuitively track how medical cannabis and other medications impact their symptoms and how this would improve their quality of life. Their main objectives were as follow:

  • 01 To explore the onboarding journey and help communicate how to best use the app and what are the benefits of tracking.
  • 02 Understand what kind of information users are interested in tracking as well as how best to visualise this data.
  • 03 To review the current app and its features.

    • What we delivered

    Deliverables

  • Research insight & findings concerning competitors, user types, and behaviour
  • Personas and scenarios
  • Experience map / user journeys
  • Information architecture
  • Design & usability recommendations for improvement
  • User flows and screen flows
  • Product sketches and wireframes
  • High fidelity mock-up
  • Prototype of design(s)
  • A final presentation to the client which summarises the UX work

    • Discover

    Competitive / Comparative Analysis

    Conducted in-depth research - to check other medical tracking apps, through this we learned that most apps are overwhelming and often not relevant to the users medical condition.

    Usability Testing

    We decided diary studies would be a good way to see how users find interacting with EVA over a few days—and how data was visually fed back to them during this time. This was conducted with three users over a period of four days. Along with the diary studies we also went ahead with usability tests to see first hand how the users interact with the app currently. We did this with four users.

    Insights from the initial test

  • “needs to hold your hand a lot more”
  • “what is the difference between Discover and Explore”
  • “when I logged my symptoms and clicked save it just went back to 0 with no confirmation so that was a big issue”
  • “I would like to be able to get reminders/notifications about specific meds”

    • Explore

    Interviews

    After deliberating with the team as to how to approach this and what questions to ask, we set up a survey as a way to gather information on tracking in general and filter through these to get our interviewees. We managed to get 9 interviews (7 people who monitor a health-related issue and 2 doctors) part-selected by our survey.

    Persona

    We gathered all our notes from the interviews and synthesised them in an affinity map, which very quickly led us to see trends that we incorporated in our primary persona Pia:

    Our insights

  • Clear onboarding is needed to help Pia when using an app
  • A lack in motivation as feedback takes time to develop
  • Personalisation is important so she gets information related to her
  • A way to spot patterns and triggers
  • To have access to her data in a clear format whenever she needs it

    • Problem statement

    “Pia needs an accessible, efficient and organised way to monitor her condition and new medication on one platform, including her symptoms, side effects and triggers, in order to predict and manage her health and wellbeing”

    User Journey

    We made a user journey to show the current experience Pia has. Here we can see the pain-points experienced so we know areas that need focusing on.

    We chose these four HMWs as they correlate with our insights

    How might we…

    Develop

    Design Studio

    Using the chosen HMW’s and our problem statement we invited our client to join us in a design studio. We prioritised onboarding as the first round of the design studio, being an important part of the whole project and something we learned was needed by users when initially opening the app. In the second round we explored how we might personalise the experience for the user.

    User Flow

    We created a user flow that will show how the user will move through the app effectively.

    Sketches

    The three areas highlighted in the flow were what we wanted to focus on, so we timeboxed ourselves and got down to sketching.

    Low-Fidelity + Usability Test

    We moved on from our sketches to create our low fidelity prototype on Figma. We conducted usability tests with 7 users.

    Test tasks

  • Sign Up + Onboarding
  • Enter Headache + Record Severity
  • Log Paracetamol, Set Reminder + Take
  • View Data
  • Add New Feature

    • What testing told us

    From this we found some great insights. Here are the results:

    Deliver

    High-Fidelity

    Due to users liking the colours and the general UI of Alta Flora which we learned in our initial testing of the app. We decided to only change what was needed. Below you can see that the design has altered but visually it’s similar.

    Custom icons + animation

    While creating our prototype I asked my team member Scarlet (who is very artistic and talented at drawing) to create custom icons for our widgets to help personalise the app. As a big fan of animation and believing that interactions can really bring delight to users when going through an app I then animated these drawings using Figma.

    High-Fidelity Testing

    Nearing the end of this design sprint we wanted to test our prototype one last time before our presentation to the client. We tested the flows with 4 users.

    “It’s all greyed out, can I use it?”

    Coloured bar to fit symptom and made an active state for ‘Save’

    “The drop down button looks like a tick, not an arrow.”

    Changing it to a filled in arrow

    “show more needs to be made more prominent”

    Making it a more prominent button, and keeping consistency in the arrow shape.

    Hitting The Brief

    Our final prototype adds onboarding/coachmarks, improved UI, personalisation and further detailed information based on the input of the user. All things we learnt users needed during our research which also met the deliverables of Alta Flora.

    Reflection

    Learnings

    Not only was this project interesting and rewarding I learned a lot throughout it. There were some tricky parts like getting the right people to interview and being able to make them feel at ease to open up about their condition and experiences. But overcoming this we learned key insights like how users wanted a more personal experience based on their condition.

    “What tracking has given me is freedom and relief, so whatever tools can help identify the triggers and patterns for your symptoms - being able to look at what’s helpful and what’s not in your routine - is helpful”
/balance:
Concept project · Wellbeing · 2 week sprint

Balance

A 2 week design sprint for the meditation app Balance. In this project I worked in a team of four. Myself, Leo Wong, Alina Tamciuc, India Berrow.

The client

Who are Balance?

Balance is a meditation app that offers personalised meditation programs based on the meditator’s experience and needs.

The brief

Brief

Balance believes that new meditators find meditation to be difficult and frustrating because their minds get distracted more easily during meditation, preventing them from enjoying the practice and creating a regular habit. Balance are considering partnering with Muse who make wearable brain sensing headbands, devices that measure brain activity using electroencephalography (EEG) sensors.

Objectives

  • 01 Understand why users can’t stay engaged and what's keeping them from building a long-term meditation habit
  • 02 Discover if using bioinformatics would increase engagement and retention
  • 03 Explore visual solutions to help display data from EEG headbands
  • 04 Pitch a user-validated prototype to Muse to begin conversations around collaboration opportunities

    • Discover

    Competitive / Comparative Analysis

    To kick things off we went ahead by doing some research about the meditation app industry. We created a feature inventory to see what competitors have to offer and compared it with Balance. We learned that Balance offers most of the features apart from Social Sharing and Group Meditation.

    Explore

    User Interviews

    We interviewed 6 users to understand the problem users are facing.

    Interview insights

  • “I find meditation difficult”
  • “I like the guided sessions”
  • “I like to measure consistency with streaks”
  • “I feel tracking makes me anxious”
  • “I'm skeptical about using bioinformatics”
  • “I can see the benefits (bioinformatics), but I'm not tempted”
  • “I would be curious to learn more about myself (using bioinformatics)”

    • Persona

    Created a persona “Penny” based off insights from research and interviews.

    Problem statement

    Penny wants to make meditation a habit to experience the benefits of a consistent practice, but finds it hard to commit.

    Develop

    Design Studio

    We got together and did a design studio bringing our ideas to light on how we each would solve Penny's problem. Voting on our favourite ideas which we would bring forward to the next stage of the process creating the low-fidelity prototype.

    User Flow

    Making a user flow was useful to show Penny's journey through the new feature on the Balance app we are trying to create.

    Low-Fidelity and User Tests

    Always so interesting moving from sketches to low-fi however due to us using the Balance app as a base we ended up being in a mid-fi instead of low-fi stage.

    Deliver

    Mid-Fidelity to High-Fidelity

    Due to our first design being more mid-fi we made adjustments to it based on the feedback we received and converted it to high-fi. Below are some of the screens from both paths Penny takes.

    Testing High-Fidelity

    We tested the high-fi prototype after implementing the feedback we received from the previous tests.

    Reflection

    Summary

    Moving forward

  • More user testing
  • Incorporate and iterate the prototype from user feedback
  • Testing out more functions we proposed but we don’t have time to do at this moment, e.g. The Thought Bin, The Chat Room Function
  • Improve the provided information about Instructors

    • Takeaway

    I learned so much during this 2 week sprint, mostly to test as much as possible. I feel we missed out on testing in the earlier stages and went to mid-fi too fast, something I will take forward in other sprints.
